new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: lines 1027-1036 (printed p.141, Appendix 'A comparative wordlist of the languages of Eastern Seram') reads: 'So unless otherwise stated the data presented below come from the following sources: Seti: Seti village / Bobot: Werinama / Masiwang: Kota Baru / Geser: Selor / Watubela: Efa / Banda: Elat / with regard to the phonetic notation, stress is penultimate unless other-wise marked.' Identical to the reported quote except capitalisation of 'with' and line-break hyphenation. I read the 300-dpi Geser-column crops : the overwhelming majority of the ~200 Geser (Selor) items carry no accent (= penultimate by the stated convention); accent-marked Geser forms seen are barém 'roof' (62…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Collins's own field transcription of Geser (Selor variant), word stress is penultimate by default; only a handful of the ~200 Geser items are marked otherwise, all with final stress (barém 'roof', malás 'long', babán 'good', na-iŋgí 'where', manlá 'how'; tái in aŋin tái 'cloud'). I.e. regular penultimate stress with a small set of lexically final-stressed words. This is a transcription convention plus data rather than a prose rule; it is independently corroborated by Visser's 2019 IPA wordlist (LexiRumah, gese1240): 375 of 425 stress-marked polysyllables penultimate, 45 final (incl. the same baˈrɛm, maˈlas, plus Malay loans and several glottal-final words).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said by Collins. (Visser 2019 marks secondary stress on the first half of reduplications, e.g. ˌlebaˈleba, ˌdahaˈlaru; data only.)
new_statements.exceptions: Marked final-stress Geser forms in Collins's list: barém, malás, babán, na-iŋgí, manlá, (aŋin) tái. Kakerissa et al. 1986 sec. 2.3 p.19 separately claim a meaning-distinguishing 'suprasegmental/prosodic feature.. untuk memberi tekanan' on /a/ and /u/ written with an apostrophe (a'ar 'root' vs ar 'chin', u'un 'knee' vs un 'empty', si'a 'cat' vs sia 'nine'), but give no stress position and the apostrophe matches a glottal stop in Visser's IPA ([ˈaʔar] 'root').
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in an elicited 200-item comparative wordlist (isolated words, some short phrases); word-level stress. Collins's statement is a notation convention applied to all six languages of the appendix, not a phonological analysis of Geser specifically.
new_statements.identity_note: Collins's Geser data are from Selor (Geser-Gorom, gese1240; variants tagged (G) Geser town, (K) Kilmuri, (P) Pulau Panjang); he uses 'Geser' for the whole Geser-Gorom language. Kakerissa et al. 1986 describe 'bahasa Gorom' from Kataloka (Gorom Laut), Amarsekaru and Lalasa (Gorom islands) = the Gorom half of the same language. Visser 2019's speakers are Geser-Gorom speakers resident in Mas (Karas Is., Fakfak, West Papua), one born in Aran, Gorom. All fall under gese1240; no separate dialect glottocodes exist.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Every one of the 20 quoted Form/Concept_ID pairs (ˈaʔar root.. ˈaula God) is present verbatim in the visser19 rows; the further forms named in rule_in_words, secondary_stress and exceptions_mentioned are all present too, with two small precisions: 'burden stick' is the compound form ai_ˌlebaˈleba (not a bare ˌlebaˈleba), and hatˈhatar / hiˈjuŋit occur only in the Comment column as 'alt.' forms, as the reader says. My own recount with the reader's convention (single-word forms, one vowel letter = one nucleus): 318 penult, 42 final, 4 antepenult (ˈaula, ˈmarani, ˈniawa, ˈsuara, all V-V sequences), 1 marked monosyllable, 98 multi-word forms and 142 unmarked forms set aside, 9 forms with a seco…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penultimate; catalog penultimate stress) and as Collins 1986 ('stress is penultimate unless otherwise marked'), now confirmed independently from a 2019 IPA field transcription of speakers with Gorom-island background rather than Collins's Selor (Geser) data; adds the set of lexical final-stress exceptions (loans plus a handful of native words, overlapping Collins's marked exceptions barém, malás, na-iŋgí, manlá) and the pattern of secondary stress on reduplications. It is primary data, not a stated rule, so it cannot be quoted as a statement of the rule.
new_statements.translation_language: IPA transcription with English concept labels
new_statements.rule_in_words: The work is a 605-item unpublished IPA wordlist and contains no sentence about stress. Counting the primary-stress mark in single-word polysyllabic forms (my count, one vowel letter = one nucleus): 318 penultimate, 42 final, 4 'antepenultimate' (all V-V sequences: ˈaula, ˈsuara, ˈniawa, ˈmarani), 1 monosyllable marked. So the default is penultimate stress with a minority of lexically final-stressed words, many of them Malay/Indonesian loans (harˈga, gemˈpa, korˈbaŋ, hutuˈba, laˈpas, paˈraŋ, taˈmaŋ, teliˈŋa, barˈsi) but also native items (baˈrɛm 'roof', maˈlas 'long', iˈluʔ 'head', iˈmaʔ 'hand', waˈnuʔ 'village', uˈʔa 'eat', gaˈhin 'good', naˈgi 'where', maˈgi 'how/why'). No obvious weight conditioning: final glottal stop occurs in both penult-stressed (ˈburaʔ, ˈhiliʔ, ˈminaʔ, ˈtiraʔ) and final-stressed (iˈluʔ, waˈnuʔ) words. The orthographic profile files (cldf/p/gese1240, cldf/p/stress) only normalise where the ˈ mark sits; they say nothing about placement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: 9 tokens carry a secondary mark, all reduplications or four-syllable words: ˌhanaˈhana 'arrow', ˌkotiˈkoti 'necklace', ˌkusuˈkusu 'thatch', ˌmesuˈmesul 'floor', ˌwalaˈwalan 'wave', ˌlebaˈleba 'burden stick', ˌdahaˈlaru 'to sail', ˌsaraˈwini 'cross-cousin', ˌtaliboˈbobar 'butterfly' (secondary on the initial or first-of-reduplicant syllable, primary on the penult). Other four-syllable words are marked with primary only (elaˈruri, hataˈhatar, rotuˈnaŋan).
new_statements.exceptions: Not stated by the source; from the transcription about 12% of polysyllabic tokens (42/364) are final-stressed, including the same two native words Collins 1986 marks as exceptions in Geser (baˈrɛm 'roof', maˈlas 'long') and loans from Malay. Comments in the data mention alternates that do not change the stress position (hataˈhatar ~ hatˈhatar 'raised platform', hiˈjugit ~ hiˈjuŋit 'to hide').
new_statements.identity_note: Visser's Geser-Gorom data (LexiRumah lect gese1240) were recorded in July 2019 in Mas village, Karas Islands, Fakfak regency, West Papua, from Fajaria Yarkuran (born 1973 in Mas; father from Mas, mother from Gorom; also speaks Kalamang) and Kasir Kilian (born 1960s in Aran, Gorom; parents from Aran and Rumeun, Gorom), i.e. a Gorom-island variety spoken in a diaspora setting. Collins 1986 (the existing catalog statement) describes the Selor (Geser island) variety, which LexiRumah files as a separate lect gese1240-geser. Both are gese1240.
